appraisal_events.evidence: "Je vois qu'au goût des propos abjects vous joignez celui des insistances vaines" and "Alors je mens ! s'écria-t-il d'un ton terrible"; the narrator names this directly as an insult, replying "vous m'insultez, je suis désarmé... la partie n'est pas égale."
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus accuses the narrator of lying and abject conduct in a violently disproportionate outburst; the narrator's own framing (unarmed, unequal contest) marks this as an unjust attack rather than a neutrally reported disagreement.

appraisal_events.evidence: Despite declaring his sympathy dead, Charlus forces the narrator to stay, offers drink and a room, and shows "une espèce de crainte un peu anxieuse" at being left alone, closing with the self-pitying Hugo quotation "Je suis veuf, je suis seul, et sur moi le soir tombe"; the narrator explicitly notes the contradiction between Charlus's claim and his behavior.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's own analysis exposes Charlus's performed anger and rejection as covering genuine neediness and fear of solitude, undercutting the authority he had just asserted.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is insulted, threatened, and effectively coerced into staying, placing him at a local disadvantage even as he verbally resists the charge.
Charlus's rage collapses into exposed loneliness and dependence on the narrator's presence, undercutting the commanding posture he displayed moments before.
Charlus shifts from imperious threat and accusation to pleading and self-pitying quotation, losing the rhetorical upper hand he held at the start of the exchange.
